This adds code to save the values of three SPRs (special-purpose
registers) used by userspace to control event-based branches (EBBs)
which are essentially interrupts that get delivered directly to
userspace.  These registers are loaded up with guest values when
entering the guest
column2: and their values are saved when exiting the

column1: guest
column2: but we were not saving the host values and restoring them

column1: before going back to userspace.
On POWER8 this would only affect userspace programs which explicitly
request the use of EBBs and also use the KVM_RUN ioctl
only source of EBBs on POWER8 is the PMU
enable bit in the PMU registers (and those PMU registers do get
properly context-switched between host and guest).  On POWER9 there
is provision for externally-generated EBBs
to the control in the PMU registers.
Since these registers only affect userspace
we first come in from userspace and restore them before returning to
userspace
column2: rather than saving/restoring the host values on every

column1: guest entry/exit.  Similarly
column2: we don't need to worry about their

column1: values on offline secondary threads since they execute in the context
of the idle task
